ALDAR CX TIME
Edition 3 · 2 November 2026 · Curated by Group CX

This week's edition is about one idea: the moment a visit stops being a transaction and becomes an experience worth leaving home for. From a cinema dome that serves each film's menu at your seat, to a museum that lets visitors choose their route by mood, to a showroom that leads with lunch rather than a sales pitch, six stories from around the world show how leading brands are designing arrival, atmosphere and belonging. Each comes with what it could mean for Aldar's destinations, communities, schools and hotels.

Read the full edition on Aldar CX Time

Signal of the week

Cosm's Shared Reality cinematic experiences
Blooloop · 2 min read

Cosm wraps classic films in 12K LED domes, themed venues and scene-timed menus, giving fans a reason to watch familiar titles together rather than at home.

Why it matters to Aldar: For Retail, it shows how a mall entertainment visit can become a destination worth leaving the sofa for, by building a shared, multi-sensory event around content people already love. For Hospitality, scene-timed themed menus point to F&B that is choreographed with the moment rather than simply served alongside it.

Also in this edition

  • Climate of Change at OMSI · Blooloop
    Portland's science museum designed a climate exhibition around how visitors feel, not just what they learn, letting them choose their route by mood and readiness.

  • Jaguar designs Knightsbridge flagship to be a physical expression of the Type 01 electric car · Dezeen
    Jaguar has turned its London showroom into a destination led by a chef's restaurant, with interiors that echo its new car and private sales spaces below.

  • Alaska Airlines Flagship Lounge by Graham Baba Architects · Retail Design Blog
    At Seattle-Tacoma airport, Alaska Airlines moves away from the exclusive business lounge, using a staged entry and four distinct zones to offer every guest a refuge.

  • Lark Hotels writes its own rules · Hospitality Design
    Lark Hotels runs more than 60 small properties across four brands, each designed around its own building, history and town rather than a single house aesthetic.

  • Light and shadow meet at One Bryant Park · Hospitality Design
    A new New York restaurant near Times Square uses Japanese ideas of filtered light and preserved shadow to turn three dining rooms into a calm retreat from the street.

Aldar CX Time is a weekly selection of the world's best experiential CX stories, each with what it means for Aldar. Every past edition stays available in the archive.
